item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Der Netzwerkausrüster Ericsson (ERICb.ST) hat im dritten Quartal einen geringeren Gewinnrückgang verbucht als von Analysten befürchtet. Effizienzverbesserungen hätten geholfen, die gestiegenen Kosten für Bauteile auszugleichen, teilte der schwedische Konzern am Donnerstag mit. Der neue Ericsson-Chef Per Narvinger warnte jedoch, dass die Kosten die Margen im kommenden Jahr belasten dürften. "Der Markt für Mobilfunknetze stagniert, die geopolitische Unsicherheit bleibt hoch und die Kosten für Bauteile sind ein Gegenwind für die Bruttomarge", erklärte Narvinger. Ericsson hatte bereits im Juli vor dem Druck durch steigende Preise für Speicherchips gewarnt, die durch die hohe Nachfrage aus dem Bereich der Künstlichen Intelligenz (KI) angetrieben werden. Im dritten Quartal schrumpfte dem Konzern zufolge der operative Gewinn vor Abschreibungen und Restrukturierungskosten auf 10,1 (Vorjahr: 15,8) Milliarden Kronen. Analysten hatten jedoch im Schnitt nur mit 7,87 Milliarden Kronen gerechnet. Die bereinigte operative Marge (Ebita) sei auf 17,0 Prozent von 28,1 Prozent gesunken, lag damit aber ebenfalls über der Analysten-Prognose von 14,2 Prozent. Auch der Umsatz mit einem organischen Zuwachs von sieben Prozent auf 59,5 Milliarden Kronen übertraf die Markterwartungen.

item.title: EEUU estudia suavizar las sanciones a la flota en la sombra, según responsable
item.description: El Gobierno de Trump está barajando la posibilidad de suavizar las sanciones contra los denominados buques de la flota en la sombra que han transportado petróleo y productos petrolíferos desde países como Rusia, Irán y Venezuela, como parte de su intento por reducir las tarifas de transporte marítimo mundiales, que se encuentran en máximos históricos, según dijo el miércoles una fuente estadounidense.
item.dc:creator: Timothy Gardner, Jarrett Renshaw
item.content:encoded: El Gobierno de Trump está barajando la posibilidad de suavizar las sanciones contra los denominados buques de la flota en la sombra que han transportado petróleo y productos petrolíferos desde países como Rusia, Irán y Venezuela, como parte de su intento por reducir las tarifas de transporte marítimo mundiales, que se encuentran en máximos históricos, según dijo el miércoles una fuente estadounidense. Las conversaciones se producen pocos días después de que el presidente Donald Trump levantara temporalmente las sanciones sobre el diésel ruso, una medida que fue objeto de una avalancha de críticas por parte del presidente ucraniano Volodímir Zelenski, de los países europeos y de algunos compañeros republicanos de Trump en el Senado de EEUU. Tanto Zelenski como los senadores estadounidenses calificaron esa medida de "regalo" al presidente ruso, Vladimir Putin, que proporcionaría a Rusia ingresos para seguir financiando su guerra en Ucrania. Las nuevas conversaciones se centran en la posibilidad de que Estados Unidos permita el transporte de "petróleo legal" en buques anteriormente sancionados, explicó el funcionario estadounidense. Esto se refiere al crudo o a los productos petrolíferos no sancionados por Washington, y no al petróleo ruso e iraní, que están sujetos a medidas punitivas. El objetivo es sacar más productos refinados y crudo del golfo Pérsico, según el funcionario. El secretario de Energía de EEUU, Chris Wright, dijo esta semana en un vídeo dirigido al Congreso Mundial del Petróleo celebrado en Riad que el Gobierno estaba barajando la posibilidad de suavizar las sanciones a los buques de la flota en la sombra, como parte de su intento por reducir las tarifas de flete, que han alcanzado niveles récord y han mermado la demanda de crudo estadounidense, según Energy Aspects, un grupo de investigación. Se difundieron fragmentos de la intervención en las redes sociales, pero Reuters no pudo obtener el vídeo completo ni una transcripción. El Departamento de Energía dijo que no estaba disponible. Las empresas que deseen utilizar los buques sancionados tendrían que solicitar autorización al Departamento del Tesoro de EEUU para hacerlo, según el funcionario. El Departamento de Energía dijo que cualquier medida para aliviar las sanciones a la flota en la sombra no ayudaría a Rusia a transportar petróleo ni productos petrolíferos. El Departamento del Tesoro remitió las preguntas al Departamento de Energía. Sin embargo, la presión de Trump para llevar rápidamente el gasóleo ruso a los mercados globales podría ejercer presión sobre los departamentos para que autoricen el transporte mediante esos buques. La Casa Blanca no respondió de inmediato a una solicitud de comentarios. Los elevados precios del petróleo y los combustibles suponen un riesgo para Trump de cara a las elecciones de mitad de mandato del 3 de noviembre, en las que los republicanos esperan mantener el control de ambas cámaras del Congreso. Trump levantó las sanciones sobre el diésel ruso hasta el 7 de abril. MÁXIMOS HISTÓRICOS Las tarifas de flete de los petroleros se han disparado hasta alcanzar máximos históricos, ya que las guerras en Irán y Ucrania han avivado la inflación y han puesto el crudo estadounidense fuera del alcance de las refinerías asiáticas, lo que las ha empujado a buscar alternativas en Oriente Medio y América Latina. Energy Aspects señaló en una nota a sus clientes que la flexibilización de las sanciones a la flota en la sombra no tendría un gran impacto en las tarifas de flete, pero podría permitir un mayor movimiento de petróleo en Oriente Medio. El levantamiento de las sanciones a los petroleros —en su mayoría antiguos y en mal estado de mantenimiento— "probablemente no aumentará de forma significativa la capacidad de la flota principal de la noche a la mañana, sobre todo porque la mayoría de los petroleros sancionados por vínculos con Rusia o Venezuela han estado operando activamente durante los últimos tres meses", se indica en la nota. La flexibilización de las restricciones "podría poner a disposición un pequeño número de petroleros adicionales para determinados viajes de ida y vuelta por (el estrecho de) Ormuz", en la vía navegable entre Irán y Omán. Es poco probable que el levantamiento de las medidas dé lugar a una relajación generalizada de las tarifas de flete, ya que las aseguradoras navieras seguirán estando sujetas a la normativa de la UE y de Reino Unido, según fuentes del sector marítimo.

item.title: TSMC-Bénéfice record pour le sixième trimestre consécutif grâce à l'IA
item.description: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) a affiché jeudi un sixième trimestre consécutif de résultats records, porté par l'essor des dépenses d'infrastructure dans le secteur technologique.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) (2330.TW) a affiché jeudi un sixième trimestre consécutif de résultats records, porté par l'essor des dépenses d'infrastructure dans le secteur technologique. Le groupe a annoncé que son bénéfice net pour le troisième trimestre s’élevait à 763,1 milliards de dollars taïwanais (21,02 milliards d'euros), en hausse de 69% sur un an et dépassant les 746,3 milliards prévus par les analystes, selon les données LSEG. Ce résultat représente le bénéfice net trimestriel le plus élevé jamais enregistré par TSMC, ainsi que son onzième trimestre consécutif de croissance du bénéfice. Selon les analystes, la demande pour les capacités de fabrication de puces d'IA du plus grand fabricant mondial de puces d'IA de pointe, ainsi que pour sa technologie avancée d'encapsulation de puces, CoWoS, reste forte. Cela a propulsé vers de nouveaux sommets l'entreprise la plus valorisée d'Asie, fournisseur clé de Nvidia (NVDA.O) et d'Apple (AAPL.O) . TSMC doit dévoiler plus tard dans la journée ses prévisions pour le quatrième trimestre et ses prévisions actualisées pour l’ensemble de l’année. La semaine dernière, l’entreprise a annoncé une hausse de 50% de son chiffre d’affaires au troisième trimestre par rapport à l’année précédente, dépassant les prévisions du marché et établissant un nouveau record. Lors de la présentation de ses résultats financiers en juillet, la société a revu à la hausse ses prévisions de dépenses d’investissement pour cette année, les portant à un montant compris entre 60 et 64 milliards de dollars, contre une fourchette précédente allant de 52 à 56 milliards de dollars.

item.title: Zelenski dice que Ucrania reanudará los ataques contra refinerías rusas, según el FT
item.description: Ucrania reanudará los ataques contra refinerías rusas, dijo el presidente ucraniano, Volodímir Zelenski, al diario británico Financial Times en una entrevista publicada el jueves.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Ucrania reanudará los ataques contra refinerías rusas, dijo el presidente ucraniano, Volodímir Zelenski, al diario británico Financial Times en una entrevista publicada el jueves. "Se ha levantado la prohibición (de atacar refinerías). Se acabó", declaró Zelenski al periódico. Criticó el afán de Washington por cerrar acuerdos comerciales con Moscú y la aparente admiración del presidente estadounidense, Donald Trump, por el ruso, Vladimir Putin, según el reporte del FT. El sábado, Trump pidió a Ucrania que sustituyera a Zelenski y arremetió contra los ataques de Ucrania a la infraestructura petrolera rusa, un día después de anunciar un acuerdo de suministro de diésel con Rusia, con el objetivo de aliviar la presión sobre los precios del combustible, que se han disparado desde que comenzó en febrero la guerra de EEUU e Israel contra Irán. Ucrania suspendió los ataques contra las refinerías de petróleo rusas y contra otras infraestructuras energéticas durante dos días tras el anuncio de Trump de un alto el fuego energético, según dijo Zelenski esta semana en X. A pesar de la tregua de Ucrania, Zelenski declaró al FT que sus fuerzas se habían quedado sin las alertas de preaviso estadounidenses sobre misiles balísticos inminentes, mientras que el servicio de comunicaciones por satélite Starlink, de Elon Musk, se había ralentizado en todo el país, lo que dificultaba las operaciones en el frente y los ataques de medio alcance contra instalaciones militares rusas. Los homólogos estadounidenses comunicaron a los mandos militares ucranianos que "si no detienen (los ataques energéticos)", bloquearán "la información de inteligencia", aunque posteriormente se presentó a Kiev como un fallo técnico, dijo Zelenski, descartando la idea de que los fallos del sistema satelital Starlink pudieran deberse a una avería. "No fue un problema técnico, fue una decisión deliberada", dijo al FT. Cuando se le preguntó si Ucrania estaría dispuesta a detener los ataques contra las instalaciones energéticas como forma de restablecer las relaciones con la Casa Blanca, respondió al periódico que solo podría aceptarlo si a cambio se le proporcionaran más misiles interceptores Patriot de fabricación estadounidense, calificándolo de "mínimo" aceptable.

item.title: Sovereign funds to turn to non-dollar bonds amid AI-driven liquidity crunch, Citi banker says
item.description: Sovereign wealth funds are increasingly raising funds outside dollar-denominated bonds as the intensifying competition to raise capital increases the costs of issuing debt, a senior banker at Citi who deals with the sector said on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Selena Li
item.content:encoded: Sovereign wealth funds are increasingly raising funds outside dollar-denominated bonds as the intensifying competition to raise capital increases the costs of issuing debt, a senior banker at Citi who deals with the sector said on Thursday. Local currency debt markets, such as the Chinese renminbi, Australian dollar, Hong Kong dollar and Singapore dollar, are drawing interest from public and private issuers looking to diversify their funding, Citi's global head of public sector group Stephanie von Friedeburg told Reuters. "There is a limited pool of capital, and for the first time in many years, the public-sector sovereigns and the private corporates are competing for that capital. And it's really being driven by sovereigns needing to borrow," she said on the sidelines of the IMF and World Bank meetings in Bangkok. Sovereign wealth funds are the world's largest group of institutional investors. Globally, their assets totalled around $16.5 trillion as of this month, according to tracking data from Global SWF. Benchmark 10-year government bond yields in the world's 10 largest developed economies have risen by an average of 81 basis points so far this year, credit rating agency Fitch [USN:L6N45Z0Y2 TEXT:"said"] earlier this week. Sovereigns and other public-sector investors are increasingly looking to issue debt to fund infrastructure, energy security, defence and development priorities, von Friedeburg said, noting that stiffer competition for funds has emerged as private capital chases AI-driven opportunities. Despite the shifts in sovereign portfolios and funding pressures, she said the US dollar will remain the dominant global reserve currency for the foreseeable future as no other market can match its depth and liquidity. With yields rising in developed markets and large amounts of private capital locked into funding AI infrastructure, von Friedeburg said there was a crowding out of developing countries, which were already facing heavy debt-service burdens and zero fiscal space. Unless innovative alternatives such as debt-for-development swaps were used, emerging markets would struggle to fund their essential energy, transport and digital futures, she added. Von Friedeburg, who works with some of the world’s largest state-backed funds, also said rising gold prices are prompting reserve managers to explore solutions such as hedging, liquidity management and borrowing against gold reserves.

item.title: Palmeiras vence a Fluminense en inicio de semifinales de Libertadores
item.description: Palmeiras sacó una ventaja de 2-1 el miércoles en su visita a Fluminense con goles del argentino José Manuel López y Marlon Freitas en un duelo de clubes brasileños en el inicio de las semifinales de la Copa Libertadores.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Palmeiras sacó una ventaja de 2-1 el miércoles en su visita a Fluminense con goles del argentino José Manuel López y Marlon Freitas en un duelo de clubes brasileños en el inicio de las semifinales de la Copa Libertadores. En el partido de ida disputado en el estadio Maracaná de Río de Janeiro, Fluminense tomó la iniciativa y mantuvo la posesión de la pelota, pero Palmeiras mostró toda su efectividad frente a la portería rival. El internacional López llegó por el segundo poste y empujó el balón a la red para abrir el marcador para el "verdao" a los 45 minutos, tras un centro bajo del uruguayo Joaquín Piquerez desde el sector izquierdo. Marlon Freitas puso el 2-0 a los 85 con un remate de voleo que venció al experimentado meta Fábio, tras una asistencia de cabeza del ingresado Felipe Anderson, El descuento de Fluminense llegó a los 94 a través de un remate de cabeza del ingresado Wesley Nata luego una salida en falso del portero Carlos Miguel. "Nos marcaron un gol en el último minuto. Creo que podríamos haber hecho un poco más, pero el fútbol es así. Tenemos que valorar la victoria en el Maracaná", dijo López tras la victoria. La revancha por un lugar en la final se disputará el miércoles en el estadio Allianz Parque de Palmeiras, en la ciudad de Sao Paulo.

item.title: POINT MARCHÉS Rechute en vue en Europe, l'IA et l'inflation américaine inquiètent (actualisé)
item.description: Les principales Bourses européennes sont attendues en repli jeudi dans une séance qui devrait à nouveau être marquée par une salve de résultats d'entreprises et des indicateurs économiques clés aux Etats-Unis alors que l'inflation outre Atlantique et le spécialiste de l'IA CoreWeave inquiètent.
item.dc:creator: Claude Chendjou
item.content:encoded: Les principales Bourses européennes sont attendues en repli jeudi dans une séance qui devrait à nouveau être marquée par une salve de résultats d'entreprises et des indicateurs économiques clés aux Etats-Unis alors que l'inflation outre Atlantique et le spécialiste de l'IA CoreWeave inquiètent. D'après les premières indications disponibles, le CAC 40 parisien (.FCHI) devrait perdre 0,48% à l'ouverture, après un gain de 0,58% mercredi. Le Dax (.GDAXI) à Francfort pourrait reculer de 0,36%, tandis que le FTSE 100 (.FTSE) à Londres devrait abandonner 0,15%. L'indice EuroStoxx 50 (.STOXX50E) est attendu en repli de 0,80% et le Stoxx 600 (.STOXX) en baisse de 0,39% au lendemain d'une hausse de 0,47%. Le marché prendra connaissance aux Etats-Unis, entre autres, des ventes au détail, des chiffres des inscriptions hebdomadaires au chômage et des prix à la production (PPI). Ces données sont cruciales dans les anticipations de l'évolution des taux directeurs alors que la probabilité d'un relèvement des coûts d'emprunt ce mois-ci de la Réserve fédérale américaine (Fed) a grimpé à près de 50% avec la publication mercredi d'un indice des prix à la consommation ([USN:L8N4601JW TEXT:"CPI"]) plus élevé que prévu. En Europe, l'économie britannique a enregistré une croissance inattendue en août, de 0,1%, selon les données officielles publiées jeudi, prolongeant une série d'indicateurs positifs de bonne augure pour le ministre des Finances, John Healey, alors qu'il prépare son budget dans un contexte financier difficile. Le marché attend désormais les chiffres définitifs de l'inflation en France. Parallèlement, le budget 2028-2034 de l'Union européenne sera au menu d'un Conseil européen qui débute ce jeudi, avec également en toile de fond le déséquilibre commercial avec la Chine. Côté publications financières, la saison des résultats se poursuit avec entre autres [USN:S8N3TR0DB TEXT:"Pernod Ricard"] et [USN:L6N4610EF TEXT:"Ericsson"]. A WALL STREET La Bourse de New York a fini en baisse mercredi, avec un net repli du Nasdaq, après la publication de données sur l'inflation ayant alimenté les craintes d'un resserrement monétaire supplémentaire de la part de la Fed, ce qui a fait plonger des titres liés à l'IA, sensibles aux taux d'intérêt. L'indice Dow Jones (.DJI) a cédé 0,09% à 51.621,48 points. Le S&P-500 (.SPX) , plus large, a perdu 1,11% à 7.718,94 points. Le Nasdaq Composite (.IXIC) a reculé de son côté de 1,88% à 26.692,87 points. EN ASIE A la [USN:L8N4610D4 TEXT:"Bourse de Tokyo"], l'indice Nikkei (.N225) a fini jeudi en baisse de 4,9% à 64.425,95 points, tandis que le Topix (.TOPX) , plus large, a cédé 2,38% à 3.999,34 points, sur fond de repli des valeurs technologiques, pénalisées par les inquiétudes liées à l'IA et à la hausse des taux d'intérêt. CoreWeave, l'opérateur américain de centres de données, spécialiste de l'IA, a plongé de 15% mercredi à Wall Street et perdait encore 6% dans les transactions hors séance, plombé par les inquiétudes sur son niveau d'endettement (50 milliards de dollars). Le rendement de ses obligations à échéance 2032 a dépassé les 15%, provoquant une onde de choc sur les marchés du crédit. Les fabricants japonais d'équipements pour semi-conducteurs Advantest (6857.T) et Tokyo Electron (8035.T) chutent respectivement de 14,36% et 7,52%. SoftBank Group (9984.T) , investisseur dans les start-ups spécialisées en IA, a dégringole de 9,08%. Le spectre de difficultés sur le marché des obligations à haut rendement, notamment pour les centres de données dont une partie du financement (et de la fragilité) provient des fournisseurs de puces, a poussé les investisseurs du monde entier vers les bons du Trésor et les obligations souveraines. "La vague de ventes en Asie ressemble moins à une détérioration soudaine des fondamentaux du secteur technologique qu'à une réévaluation du coût du capital", explique Charu Chanana, cheffe stratège en investissements chez Saxo Bank, à Singapour. "Les investisseurs ne remettent pas en cause l'existence d'une demande en matière d'IA", a-t-elle ajouté. "Ils s'interrogent de plus en plus sur le prix qu'ils devraient payer pour cette croissance alors que les taux d'intérêt sont élevés, volatils et susceptibles de remonter". L'indice MSCI regroupant les valeurs d'Asie et du Pacifique (hors Japon) (.MIAPJ0000PUS) recule de 3,3%, avec notamment une chute de 8% du Kospi sud-coréen (.KS11) . Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) (2330.TW) recule de 2,01%, Samsung Electronics (005930.KS) de 10,99%, tandis que les fabricants de puces mémoire SK Hynix (000660.KS) et Kioxia Holdings (285A.T) cèdent respectivement 12,61% et 13,04%. En Chine, le SSE Composite (.SSEC) de Shanghai fléchit de 2,01% et le CSI 300 (.CSI300) reflue de 1,95%, avec notamment un plongeon de 2,81% du compartiment technologique (.STAR50) . A Hong Kong, l'indice Hang Seng (.HSI) abandonne 1,44%, avec un repli de 2,99% du secteur de la "tech" (.HSTECH) . LES VALEURS A SUIVRE EN EUROPE: [USN:L8N46020W] CHANGES Le dollar recule de 0,43% face à un panier de devises de référence (.DXY) , après avoir atteint mercredi son plus haut niveau en 18 mois, effaçant une partie des gains enregistrés après la publication mercredi de chiffres d'inflation plus élevés que prévu. L'euro rebondit de 0,47%, à 1,1208 dollar, après être tombé à son plus bas niveau en 18 mois, à 1,1223 dollars, La livre sterling s'échange à 1,3242 dollar, en hausse de 0,37%, redressant après avoir touché la veille un plus bas en 13 mois. TAUX Le rendement des bons du Trésor américain à dix ans est pratiquement stable jeudi, à 5,11%, après une forte volatilité la veille où il est descendu à 5,19% après avoir grimpé en séance à 5,32%. Les marchés se sont détournés du risque, la forte hausse du CPI américain ayant renforcé les anticipations de taux d'intérêt élevés et durables de la Fed et ravivé les inquiétudes concernant le lourd endettement des entreprises d'IA, ce qui a entraîné des flux de capitaux vers les actifs refuge souverains. Les investisseurs suivront les déclarations des responsables de la Fed, notamment du président Kevin Warsh, lors des réunions annuelles du FMI et de la Banque mondiale à Bangkok ce jeudi, afin de déceler des indices sur la prochaine décision de la banque centrale américaine. Le rendement du Bund allemand à dix ans cède environ sept points de base, à 3,39%, après avoir fini quasiment stable la veille. PÉTROLE Le marché pétrolier est en repli jeudi alors que les investisseurs examinent les perspectives d'approvisionnement et les tensions au Moyen-Orient. Les Etats-Unis [USN:L6N461003 TEXT:"envisagent"] d'alléger les sanctions contre les navires de la "flotte fantôme", qui transportent notamment du pétrole en provenance de pays comme la Russie, l'Iran ou le Venezuela, afin de faire baisser les taux de fret mondiaux, qui ont atteint des niveaux records, a dit mercredi un responsable américain. item.title: Sancionan al Rayo Vallecano con el cierre parcial de su estadio tras la suspensión de un partido
item.description: El comité de disciplina de la Real Federación Española de Fútbol (RFEF) sancionó el miércoles al Rayo Vallecano con el cierre parcial de su estadio y una multa de 6.000 euros (6.687 dólares), después de que las protestas de aficionados obligaran a suspender su partido contra el Athletic de Bilbao.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El comité de disciplina de la Real Federación Española de Fútbol (RFEF) sancionó el miércoles al Rayo Vallecano con el cierre parcial de su estadio y una multa de 6.000 euros (6.687 dólares), después de que las protestas de aficionados obligaran a suspender su partido contra el Athletic de Bilbao. El encuentro del sábado se interrumpió a los 13 minutos, después de que aficionados lanzaran repetidamente aviones de papel y pelotas de goma al terreno de juego en protesta contra el propietario del club, Raúl Martín Presa. El comité ordenó al Rayo cerrar la tribuna sur en su próximo partido de liga como local, contra el Elche el 24 de octubre. Advirtió de que la repetición de incidentes similares podría dar lugar al cierre de todo el estadio. LaLiga aún no ha anunciado cuándo se reanudará el partido contra el Athletic. Las protestas contra Presa son cada vez más frecuentes, alimentadas por el malestar ante lo que los aficionados consideran un abandono de las instalaciones del club. Los jugadores y el cuerpo técnico del Rayo emitieron un comunicado en febrero en el que afirmaban que la ciudad deportiva y el terreno de juego de su estadio no reunían las condiciones necesarias para su uso. Posteriormente, el Gobierno de la Comunidad de Madrid suspendió el uso del estadio de Vallecas por parte del club por motivos de seguridad, lo que obligó al Rayo a disputar en otros recintos sus tres primeros partidos como local de esta temporada de LaLiga. El Rayo rechazó las afirmaciones de que el estadio no era seguro y señaló que las inspecciones técnicas y dos auditorías habían determinado que cumplía las normas exigidas de seguridad y salud pública. Presa dijo el mes pasado a la Cadena COPE que el estadio de Vallecas estaba en una "situación óptima" y que los aficionados no corrían ningún riesgo. El Rayo dijo el sábado que identificaría y sancionaría a los responsables de los incidentes que interrumpieron el partido contra el Athletic, y acusó al grupo que organizó la protesta de llevar a cabo una campaña sostenida contra el club. El Rayo ocupa el puesto 13 de LaLiga con ocho puntos. Su próximo partido será el lunes de visitante contra el Getafe. (1 dólar = 0,8973 euros)

item.title: Klingbeil: Ukraine muss trotz Krieg noch stärker Reformen umsetzen
item.description: Bundesfinanzminister Lars Klingbeil fordert von der Ukraine weitere Reformen. Dennoch gebe es die klare Erwartung, dass die von Russland angegriffene Ukraine trotz des Krieges Reformen vorantreiben müsse. Sie dürfe dabei nicht nachlassen. "Ich glaube, da geht es noch besser."

item.content:encoded: Bundesfinanzminister Lars Klingbeil fordert von der Ukraine weitere Reformen. "Unsere Unterstützung für die Ukraine ist klar, da wird auch nicht gewackelt", sagte der SPD-Chef am Donnerstag in Bangkok am Rande der Herbsttagung des Internationalen Währungsfonds (IWF) zu Journalisten. Dennoch gebe es die klare Erwartung, dass die von Russland angegriffene Ukraine trotz des Krieges Reformen vorantreiben müsse. Sie dürfe dabei nicht nachlassen. "Ich glaube, da geht es noch besser." Konkrete Beispiele nannte Klingbeil nicht, erwähnte aber, dass er die milliardenschwere Finanzierung der Ukraine in Deutschland rechtfertigen müsse. Korruption ist seit langem ein großes Problem in der Ukraine. Klingbeil ergänzte, Russland habe die Angriffe auf die Ukraine zuletzt noch verstärkt. Er werbe dafür, eine ausreichende Finanzierung der Ukraine für 2026 und 2027 zu sichern. Die Finanzminister der 20 führenden Industrie- und Schwellenländer (G20) haben sich am Donnerstag am Rande der IWF-Tagung zu Beratungen getroffen. Dabei war auch Klingbeils russischer Amtskollege Anton Siluanow, wie schon bei einem Treffen Ende August. Klingbeil sagte, er habe nicht mit ihm geredet und Russland schon im August offen kritisiert. Er sei kein normaler Partner. "Russland muss diesen Krieg stoppen."

item.title: Professional surfer suspended by second body over 'allegations of abuse'
item.description: The International Surfing Association (ISA) has joined the World Surf League (WSL) in provisionally suspending a male professional surfer over what it described as "serious allegations of abuse within the surfing community".
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The International Surfing Association (ISA) has joined the World Surf League (WSL) in provisionally suspending a male professional surfer over what it described as "serious allegations of abuse within the surfing community". The WSL suspended the surfer, who it said was competing on its men's championship tour, earlier this week over his alleged conduct at a "private gathering" in Tahiti in August following the conclusion of the Tahiti Pro leg of the circuit. The ISA, which is the international governing body for surfing and organises the Olympic competition, issued a statement late on Wednesday. "The ISA Executive Committee has decided to provisionally suspend the athlete concerned from participating in ISA-sanctioned events, pending further investigation and review in accordance with the ISA's applicable rules and safeguarding procedures," it read. "This precautionary decision has been taken in the interest of athlete safety and welfare, and does not constitute a determination of wrongdoing. "The ISA firmly believes that all athletes have the right to participate in sport in a safe and respectful environment, free from harassment, violence, and abuse of any kind." The ISA said it would make no further comment on the allegations at this stage. The WSL said it was continuing to follow its process and had offered assistance to relevant authorities. French Polynesian police did not immediately respond to an enquiry from Reuters about whether an investigation had been launched into the alleged incident in Tahiti.

Die Bundesregierung rechnet - wie der IWF auch - für dieses Jahr mit einem Wachstum von 1,3 Prozent, nächstes Jahr dann 1,1 Prozent. Klingbeil sagte, die Prognosen gäben Anlass zu vorsichtigem Optimismus. Der Staat könne es aber nicht alleine richten. "Wir geben den Impuls." Nächste Woche plant die Regierung eine große Investorenkonferenz in Berlin und damit ein Zeichen für mehr private Investitionen. Diese fehlen seit langem. Die Wirtschaft beklagt schlechte Rahmenbedingungen in Deutschland - durch zu viel Bürokratie sowie hohe Steuern und Energiekosten. Klingbeil sagte, es brauche deswegen Reformen, die die Regierung jetzt auch angehe.

item.title: TSMC registra su sexto trimestre consecutivo de ganancias récord gracias al auge de la IA
item.description: TSMC, el mayor fabricante mundial de chips avanzados de inteligencia artificial, reportó el jueves su sexto trimestre consecutivo de ganancias récord, impulsadas por el fuerte aumento del gasto en infraestructura del sector tecnológico.
item.dc:creator: Wen-Yee Lee, Ben Blanchard
item.content:encoded: TSMC, el mayor fabricante mundial de chips avanzados de inteligencia artificial, reportó el jueves su sexto trimestre consecutivo de ganancias récord, impulsadas por el fuerte aumento del gasto en infraestructura del sector tecnológico. Analistas afirman que sigue siendo sólida la demanda de capacidad de fabricación de chips de IA de Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co (TSMC) (2330.TW) , así como de su tecnología de encapsulado avanzado de chips, CoWoS. Esto ha llevado a nuevas cotas a la empresa más valiosa de Asia, un proveedor clave de Nvidia (NVDA.O) y Apple (AAPL.O) . Su capitalización bursátil ronda los dos billones de dólares, casi el doble que la de su competidor surcoreano Samsung Electronics (005930.KS) . TSMC dijo que su ganancia neta en el trimestre de julio a septiembre alcanzó los 763.100 millones de dólares taiwaneses (23.590 millones de dólares estadounidenses), un 69% más que un año antes y por encima de la estimación SmartEstimate de LSEG de 746.300 millones de dólares taiwaneses, elaborada a partir de las previsiones de 16 analistas. La conferencia en la que presentará sus previsiones para el cuarto trimestre y actualizará las del conjunto del año está programada para las 0600 GMT. Los inversores la seguirán de cerca, después de que la preocupación por nuevas subidas de las tasas de interés de la Reserva Federal estadounidense golpeara el miércoles a las acciones vinculadas a la IA, sensibles al aumento de los costos de financiación. Las acciones de TSMC que cotizan en Taipéi cerraron el jueves con una caída del 2% antes de la publicación de los resultados, mientras que el índice de referencia (.TWII) retrocedió un 3,4%. El resultado supuso la mayor ganancia neta trimestral de la historia de TSMC, así como su undécimo trimestre consecutivo de crecimiento de las ganancias. La semana pasada, la empresa anunció un aumento interanual del 50% de sus ingresos del tercer trimestre, con lo que superó las previsiones del mercado y alcanzó un nuevo récord. TSMC está invirtiendo 265.000 millones de dólares en la construcción de fábricas de chips en el estado estadounidense de Arizona, incluidos otros 100.000 millones anunciados en julio. En septiembre, Reuters informó de que TSMC estaba evaluando una posible inversión en Texas. El consejero delegado de Tesla, Elon Musk, también dijo la semana pasada que sus empresas construirían y operarían el complejo de chips de IA Terafab, del que TSMC podría subarrendar una parte. En la conferencia de resultados de julio, la empresa elevó su previsión de inversión de capital para este año a entre 60.000 y 64.000 millones de dólares, frente a su estimación anterior, que la situaba en el extremo superior de un rango de entre 52.000 y 56.000 millones. ASML (ASML.AS) , el mayor fabricante mundial de equipos para producir chips de IA y semiconductores avanzados, [USN:L6N4600C6 TEXT:"dijo el miércoles"] que sus clientes ya buscaban realizar pedidos para 2029 y 2030, lo que aliviaba las preocupaciones de que el auge de la inversión en IA estuviera perdiendo impulso. Las acciones de TSMC que cotizan en Taipéi acumulaban una subida del 57% en lo que va de año, en línea con el avance del 62% del mercado taiwanés en su conjunto. (1 dólar = 32,3450 dólares taiwaneses)

item.title: Seventeen students, one teacher killed in school roof collapse in Pakistan
item.description: At least 17 students, all of them below the age of 13, and one teacher were killed in a school roof collapse in Pakistan's Peshawar city, a local hospital spokesperson said on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: At least 17 students, all of them below the age of 13, and one teacher were killed in a school roof collapse in Pakistan's Peshawar city, a local hospital spokesperson said on Thursday. The students and the teacher were brought dead to the Lady Reading Hospital along with more than a dozen people who were injured in the incident, hospital spokesperson Mohammad Asim said. The cause of the collapse was not immediately clear.

item.title: TotalEnergies flags Q3 profit surge as Iran war continues to drive energy prices
item.description: TotalEnergies expects its refining margins to have nearly quadrupled in the third quarter compared to last year, as the Iran war continues to lift energy prices and boost profits for oil majors, the French company said in a trading update on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: TotalEnergies (TTEF.PA) expects its refining margins to have nearly quadrupled in the third quarter compared to last year, as the Iran war continues to lift energy prices and boost profits for oil majors, the French company said in a trading update on Thursday. The US-Israeli war with Iran , which led to the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz, has disrupted global supplies and pushed crude oil and gas prices to multi-year highs, delivering a windfall for major energy companies like Total. TotalEnergies expects to report a refining margin of $33.2 per barrel for the July-September quarter, up from $13.5 a barrel in the previous three months, and almost four times the $8.4 per barrel it had posted a year ago. Rival Shell (SHEL.L) [USN:L4N45T0DM TEXT:"said"] last week it expected a record-high third-quarter refining margin, while BP (BP.L) [USN:L6N45Z0CU TEXT:"said"] on Tuesday its refining margin was set to triple from last year. TotalEnergies and Shell will report detailed third-quarter results on October 29, with BP to follow a day later.

item.title: UK economy beats forecasts again to grow 0.1% in August
item.description: Britain's economy grew unexpectedly in August, official data showed on Thursday, extending a run of resilient data that will encourage finance minister John Healey as he prepares his budget against a tough financial backdrop.
item.dc:creator: Andy Bruce
item.content:encoded: Britain's economy grew unexpectedly in August, official data showed on Thursday, extending a run of resilient data that will encourage finance minister John Healey as he prepares his budget against a tough financial backdrop. The Office for National Statistics reported a 0.1% increase in gross domestic product in August, stronger than the consensus forecast in a Reuters poll of economists for a 0.1% drop. The annual growth rate picked up to 2.1%, the strongest reading since October 2022 when output was bouncing back from the COVID-19 pandemic. Excluding that period, it was the strongest reading since December 2019. Adding to signs that the artificial intelligence boom is boosting Britain's economy, the ONS said computer programming was the largest contributor to growth in the three months to August. But it also pointed to broad-based growth over the past year across the services sector that dominates Britain's economy. For August alone, growth was driven by the manufacturing sector which showed a 1.2% month-on-month surge, defying forecasts for a small drop in output. The services sector was flat, but still beat forecasts for a 0.1% dip, while construction output fell slightly.

item.title: Zelenskiy says Ukraine will resume strikes on Russian refineries, FT reports
item.description: Ukraine will resume strikes on Russian refineries, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy told the Financial Times in an interview published on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Ukraine will resume strikes on Russian refineries, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy told the Financial Times in an interview published on Thursday. “The block (on attacking refineries) is out. We’re done,” Zelenskiy told the newspaper. He was critical of Washington’s eagerness to strike business deals with Moscow and US President Donald Trump’s apparent admiration for Russia’s Vladimir Putin, the FT report said. Trump on Saturday [USN:L6N45W06G TEXT:"called for"] Ukraine to replace Zelenskiy and railed against Ukraine's attacks on Russian oil infrastructure, one day after announcing a diesel supply deal with Russia, aiming to ease pressure on fuel prices that have soared since the US-Israeli war with Iran began in February. Ukraine halted strikes on Russian oil refineries and its other energy infrastructure for two days following Trump's announcement of an energy ceasefire, Zelenskiy said earlier this week on X. Despite Ukraine’s pause, Zelenskiy told the FT his forces had been left without US early-warning alerts for incoming ballistic missiles, while Elon Musk’s Starlink satellite communications service had been slowed down across the country, hampering frontline operations and medium-range strikes against Russian military sites. Ukrainian military officials were told by their US counterparts that “if you will not stop (the energy strikes), we will block intelligence”, although it was subsequently presented to Kyiv as a technical glitch, Zelenskiy said, dismissing the idea that failures of the Starlink satellite system might have been caused by a fault. “It was not a technical problem, it was the will,” he told the FT. Asked whether Ukraine would be open to halting energy strikes as a way of repairing relations with the White House, he told the newspaper he could only agree if in return he was given more US-made Patriot interceptors, calling it the “minimum” that would be acceptable.

item.title: Oil's long view darkens as Iran war refuses to end
item.description: Oil markets initially treated the Iran war as a brief bullish disruption in a long-term bearish trend. But traders are now betting that oil prices will remain elevated through 2028, forcing a rethink of the global inflation outlook.
item.dc:creator: Ron Bousso
item.content:encoded: Oil markets initially treated the Iran war as a brief bullish disruption in a long-term bearish trend. But traders are now betting that oil prices will remain elevated through 2028, forcing a rethink of the global inflation outlook. Eight months into the war, the buffers that helped absorb the initial energy shock – most notably onshore crude oil stockpiles – are wearing dangerously thin. At the same time, the recovery in crude exports through the Strait of Hormuz remains [USN:L8N45Z15J TEXT:"fragile"], global refining capacity has been eroded and credible diplomatic pathways to end the conflict appear narrower than ever. Global benchmark Brent [USN:L1N46000C TEXT:"crude futures"] tell the story. Contracts for delivery in December 2027 have climbed more than 13% since the start of September to $86 a barrel, the highest level for the contract, while December 2026 contracts have gained around 12%. The Brent forward curve is not a price forecast, of course. But it reflects the willingness of refiners, airlines, commodity traders and asset managers to lock in elevated prices months and even years into the future. In effect, market participants are paying a premium against the possibility that today's disruptions will become tomorrow's normal. SUPPLY RECOVERY This market positioning stands in stark contrast to widely held industry expectations of a recovery in global oil supplies next year. The International Energy Agency projects global supply will rise to 108.3 million barrels per day (bpd) in 2027 from 100.7 million bpd this year as Middle Eastern exports recover. Demand, meanwhile, is forecast to increase from 102.4 million bpd to 104.4 million bpd next year, still slightly below 2025 consumption. This recovery is expected to be concentrated in petrochemical feedstocks rather than transportation fuels like diesel. Regardless, the agency's projected balances imply a sizeable supply surplus next year that would normally weigh on prices. Yet the steady rise in long-dated futures suggests investors are increasingly sceptical that this recovery will fully materialise or, if it does, that it will endure. The standoff between Washington and Tehran remains centred on control of the Strait of Hormuz. While oil flows through the strategic waterway have rebounded to near pre-war levels in recent weeks thanks partly to US naval support, Iran has [USN:L8N45Z15J TEXT:"intensified attacks"] on vessels in the past week and threatened further disruption. The conflict has also expanded beyond the Gulf. Yemen's Iran-aligned [USN:L6N4600LK TEXT:"Houthis"] have recently stepped up missile and drone attacks on Saudi Arabia, including [USN:L6N4600LI TEXT:"strikes this week"] on the headquarters of Saudi Arabia's state-owned oil giant Aramco (2222.SE) in Dhahran. Given this backdrop, every barrel leaving the Gulf now carries a widening security premium. Complex logistics, elevated freight rates, high insurance costs and military protection now account for nearly a third of the cost of moving a barrel of oil out of the region, compared with 3% before the war. Absent a durable settlement over Hormuz, much of that cost is likely to remain entrenched in prices for the foreseeable future. DIESEL ON FIRE The strain is even more visible in diesel markets. Benchmark European diesel futures hit a record $1,480 per metric ton, equivalent to around $210 per barrel, in mid-September amid an acute shortage of supplies caused by [USN:L6N4600HF TEXT:"disruptions"] in the Middle East and Russia. Since Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine , drone attacks by Kyiv have crippled Russian refineries, forcing Moscow to ban diesel exports earlier this year. US President Donald Trump on Friday announced [USN:L4N45Y0AR TEXT:"an agreement"] with Russian President Vladimir Putin to allow Moscow to resume some diesel exports and later proclaimed another “energy ceasefire” between Russia and Ukraine. But the additional Russian exports cited by Trump are minuscule – equivalent to roughly 12 hours of global supply – and no one, including the two parties involved, is [USN:L6N45Y0SD TEXT:"giving much credence"] to the purported ceasefire. Instead, traders are focused on the dramatic loss of fuel production capacity this year, with diesel futures signalling continued tightness ahead. Contracts for delivery in December 2027 climbed above $1,000 a ton for the first time this week, compared with a pre-war level of $644. The fuel repricing may ultimately prove more important than the rise in crude itself. Diesel powers the trucks, ships, factories and farms that underpin global commerce. Sustained diesel inflation has historically seeped into the wider economy through higher transportation, manufacturing and food costs. With headline [USN:L1N45Z121 TEXT:"US inflation"] running at 3.7% in September – almost twice the Federal Reserve’s targeted 2% rate – and core inflation creeping up, persistently high diesel prices remain a major concern for US and global policymakers. A NEW REALITY For much of this year, energy markets operated on the assumption that the Iran war would resemble past geopolitical crises: a sharp but temporary disruption followed by a quick return to normality. Increasingly, investors are concluding otherwise. The issue is no longer simply how much oil can move through Hormuz. Markets need to know whether the global energy system can quickly rebuild the inventories, refinery capacity and supply chains damaged by months of conflict. Until then, the world risks becoming trapped in an era of structurally higher energy costs that lasts long after the shooting stops. item.title: AI investment boom may be papering over US economic cracks
item.description: Strip away the AI blanket and you may find the rest of the economy shivering underneath. Even if the reality is less stark, the latest research shows AI heat in national accounts is mirrored by cold spots elsewhere.
item.dc:creator: Mike Dolan
item.content:encoded: Strip away the AI blanket and you may find the rest of the economy shivering underneath. Even if the reality is less stark, the latest research shows AI heat in national accounts is mirrored by cold spots elsewhere. There's little doubt about the contribution to overall US gross domestic product from the frenzied boom in AI investment, financing and infrastructure building. Most estimates show that about a third of economic growth over the past couple of years is due to the AI buildout, and almost a quarter of all US imports last year were AI-related goods. And, depending on how you define it, AI-related stocks now account for about half of the S&P 500 (.SPX) market capitalization. But New York Federal Reserve economist Julian di Giovanni this week focused on the fact that the surge in AI-related imports over the past two years had not materially widened the trade and current account deficits, as might be expected. In explaining why, he framed the issue in terms of how the current account is a balance of savings and investment, suggesting an investment spending spree or a jump in tech equipment imports need not affect the overall balance if domestic savings are sufficient to fund the additional investment. In economics terms, the current account balance is a country's gross savings minus its gross domestic investment. Mapping savings and investment over the past six years since the COVID-19 pandemic shows the current account gap did indeed widen up to early last year, but has since narrowed during a wave of tariffs from the incoming Donald Trump administration. However, most of the widening deficit of recent years was due to a drop in savings rather than gross investment spending, di Giovanni points out in the Liberty Street Economics blog. In fact, aggregate investment as a share of GDP has been basically unchanged for eight years at just under 22% and has shown no particular change since the AI capital expenditure boom took off in earnest after 2023. Gross domestic investment averaged 21.3% of GDP in the five years before the pandemic and 21.5% in the three years since the ChatGPT launch that sparked the frenzy. PHANTOM INVESTMENT BOOM? Di Giovanni's main point is that while investment in information technology, equipment and software has risen, it has been offset by declines elsewhere, including weaker factory construction since 2022, residential investment and spending on structures and equipment outside data centers and technology equipment. Household saving is down slightly in recent years, due in part to wealth effects from higher equity values, but it's fallen much less than it did during the dotcom expansion in the late 1990s. Business saving has barely fallen, unlike the dotcom era, and that's likely due to the drawdown so far of hefty cash positions by the hyperscalers doing the bulk of the capex. Government "dis-saving", or widening government budget deficits, has moved in the opposite direction over the past few years and marks another stark contrast to the late 1990s boom. Government dis-saving accounts for 1.75 points of the 2.4 percentage-point increase in the current account deficit since the pandemic, with falling private savings adding about half a point and business investment contributing next to nothing. "Changes in fiscal policy have been the major driver of current account dynamics, with a smaller role played by private saving and no discernible investment channel," di Giovanni concluded, adding the caveat that a ramping up of debt- and equity-financed spending from here could yet change the picture. Beyond the balance of payments dynamics, though, the obvious question is just how much relative weakness the AI boom is covering up and how much of a cyclical downswing the economy and markets might now be suffering in its absence. With so much riding on AI delivering, the temptation is to treat it as "too big to fail." But if a sudden slowdown in the AI boom, an accident or shock in financing, or a massive stock sell-off were to hit, the economy would go south along with it — and it's not hard to see why. item.title: Is the AI rout making bonds safe again?
item.description: A rude awakening over the debt-fuelled AI binge has sent investors rushing out of stocks and into government bonds, which now seem to be reclaiming their status as a safe haven and a hedge against equity and credit market wobbles.
item.dc:creator: Ankur Banerjee, Tom Westbrook
item.content:encoded: A [USN:L6N45Z12J TEXT:"rude awakening"] over the debt-fuelled AI binge has sent investors rushing out of [USN:L6N460140 TEXT:"stocks"] and into government bonds, which now seem to be reclaiming their status as a safe haven and a hedge against equity and credit market wobbles. For much of the year, bonds have offered little protection as inflationary pressure pushed borrowing costs to multi-decade highs, leaving investors warily looking to hedge funds and other assets as alternatives. But on Wednesday, something strange happened: Treasuries and other government bonds rallied sharply, despite a hotter-than-expected US inflation report, which left chances of a US rate hike from the Federal Reserve this year on the table. The bigger concern for investors now is whether massive AI spending will pay off soon enough, especially with inflation running hot, and how much longer companies will be able to continue to raise funds at current costs of capital. Credit markets are also showing strain, with the cost of insuring some AI-exposed companies against default [USN:L4N4610DV TEXT:"hitting"] records. "The upside surprise in US CPI and the subsequent rally in bonds is highly counter-intuitive," said Prashant Newnaha, senior rates strategist at TD Securities. "The cleanest read through is that the slump in AI is repricing growth expectations down leading to bonds serving as a hedge for stocks," he said. On Thursday, the yield on the benchmark US 10-year Treasury note fell 8.4 basis points to 5.105%, hitting its lowest level in three weeks and easing away from the 24-year high it touched last week. The benchmark 10-year JGB yield dropped 6.5 bps to 2.93%, the lowest since September 10. Futures for German bunds and French OATs were up 0.7% Wagers on a near-term move were also tempered after San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly said further hikes would probably be needed but signalled no need to act at the October 27-28 meeting. AI TRADE UNWINDS The question left for investors, who remain unsettled by high volatility for rates, is whether an asset that's been dragged by soaring sovereign debt and hot inflation is capable of offering a cushion if equities start to take a bigger tumble. Treasury yields posted their sharpest quarterly rise since 1994 in the July-September period. "Bond-equity correlation is definitely fracturing," said Damien Boey, portfolio strategist at Wilson Asset Management in Sydney. "Usually, growth stocks do well in particular when bond yields fall, but last night growth stocks doing badly drove a safe-haven bid for bonds and their yields lower." Earlier this week, BlackRock Investment Institute [USN:L1N45Z07S TEXT:"downgraded"] its view on US stocks to neutral, citing volatility around AI, and upgraded Treasuries, preferring short-term notes. The rout has been building for days as investors get increasingly nervous about AI spending. The selloff in global equities centred on AI stocks that have powered the markets to record highs in recent years. South Korea's KOSPI (.KS11) , an epicentre of the AI boom, sank 8%, set for its seventh straight decline. The Philadelphia SE Semiconductor Index (.SOX) dropped 4.3% on Wednesday, down for a sixth straight session, its longest losing streak since May 2025. "Investors are separating AI companies with deep cash flows from those that need debt to build," said Kenneth Goh, UOB Kay Hian's director of private wealth management. "Private credit is where it could spread next," Goh said. "Listed lenders to tech and venture companies already trade at steep discounts to their asset values, and more cautious lenders can slow the AI build-out well before any defaults appear." Selling this week has been particularly intense in data centre operator [USN:L4N4601XL TEXT:"CoreWeave"] (CRWV.O) , which has issued $22 billion of bonds and $26 billion of loans, according to LSEG data. "Much of the spending is by companies borrowing to rent computing power to AI labs that don't yet earn enough to cover the bill," said Armina Rosenberg, portfolio manager at Minotaur Capital. "When CoreWeave's bonds yield 15%, investors are asking whether the end customers will make enough money to keep paying in three or four years," she said.

item.title: Germany's Klingbeil says support for Ukraine comes with reform expectations
item.description: German Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil said on Thursday his country's support for Ukraine was clear but came with expectations for political reforms.
item.dc:creator: Maria Martinez
item.content:encoded: German Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil said on Thursday his country's support for Ukraine was clear but came with expectations for political reforms. "Our support for Ukraine is clear. There is no wavering on that. But there are also clear expectations of the Ukrainian government," Klingbeil told reporters on the sidelines of IMF-World Bank meetings in Bangkok. "I think there is room for improvement." "That is also an expectation because we must repeatedly explain to German citizens why support for Ukraine is so substantial," he added, given cuts in the German budget. The EU has pledged €45 billion ($50 billion) for Ukraine for 2027, but the country's needs will be much higher and the [USN:L8N4600YW TEXT:"EU is scrambling"] to organise financial support from countries such as Norway, Switzerland, Canada, Japan or Britain. Klingbeil said he was discussing with international partners how to ensure Ukraine's financing, with commitments from Australia and South Korea during meetings on Thursday in Bangkok. "One has to say that this is a different kind of commitment from that of us Europeans, who are geographically much closer," Klingbeil said. "But both made very clear that their support for Ukraine will continue."

item.title: Indonesia blames peatland degradation for raging fires, vows restoration
item.description: Indonesia has blamed peatland degradation by past food estates for its worst wildfire season in 11 years, and will work to restore its peat ecosystem, a senior official said on Thursday as thick haze continued to blanket its cities and drift into neighbouring countries.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Indonesia has blamed peatland degradation by past food estates for its worst wildfire season in 11 years, and will work to restore its peat ecosystem, a senior official said on Thursday as thick haze continued to blanket its cities and drift into neighbouring countries. The Southeast Asian nation is struggling to put out its most intense wildfire since 2015 after an El Niño-driven drought made its forests and land highly flammable. The fires have been raging for months and hundreds of thousands of people have contracted respiratory illnesses in seven Indonesian provinces alone. The transboundary haze has also polluted the air in [USN:L6N4600NO TEXT:"neighbouring countries"], with schools suspended in East Timor and some states of Malaysia. Indonesian cities, especially in Sumatra and Kalimantan, are being choked by haze, with the air pollution index far exceeding the "hazardous" level of 300. The Katingan district of Central Kalimantan had a reading of nearly 1,600 earlier on Thursday, while the provincial capital Palangka Raya recorded nearly 1,300. Central Kalimantan and South Sumatra are currently the worst affected areas due to peatland fires, which smoulder slowly beneath the surface and can re-emerge anytime, and also produce thicker smoke. "As a result of long-standing interventions, the peatlands in Central Kalimantan and South Sumatra have suffered serious degradation. Massive drainage efforts were carried out, fundamentally altering the natural properties of the peat," said deputy food minister Hanif Faisol Nurofiq, identifying a food estate project in the 1990s as one of the causes of degradation. "Today, a large portion of these peatlands has been destroyed," he said. Peatland protection group Pantau Gambut estimated that out of 24 million hectares of Indonesian peatland, 16 million hectares have been made more fire-prone as a result of ecosystem damage, including extensive deforestation and the depletion of water tables. A 2024 study conducted by Pantau Gambut showed that only 3% of the peatland damaged by fires over the 2015-2019 period has been restored into forest, while 54% was converted into monoculture plantations, mainly oil palm. The government is aiming to drill wells to rewet peatlands and improve water canal management, Hanif said. "It is quite simple, yet we have forgotten, neglected, or failed to carry it out," he said. Dozens of residents of Palangka Raya, which has been swathed in thick orange smog this week, staged a protest at its governor's office on Thursday, calling for the situation to be handled more effectively, local news reported. "The sky yesterday was very yellow ... People's activities are far reduced because of this condition. We hope there will be rain soon that will ease this problem," a 46-year-old Palangka Raya resident named Adinata told Reuters.

item.title: Kenya raises fuel prices as Middle East conflict lifts import costs
item.description: Kenya raised the maximum retail prices of petrol and diesel on Wednesday, the energy regulator said, citing higher import costs linked to the conflict in the Middle East.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Kenya raised the maximum retail prices of petrol and diesel on Wednesday, the energy regulator said, citing higher import costs linked to the conflict in the Middle East. Kenya hiked petrol prices by 6% and diesel prices by 4.5%, with the East African nation relying on the Middle East region for nearly all of its fuel supplies A litre of diesel will cost 227.76 Kenyan shillings ($1.76) in the capital city of Nairobi, from 217.86 shillings, while kerosene will rise to 219.87 shillings from 191.38 shillings between October 15 and November 14, when new prices will be announced. The energy regulator said the government extended a reduction in value-added tax on fuel to 8% from 16% until January 14. Fuel prices affect multiple sectors including transport, agriculture and construction. ($1 = 129.6000 Kenyan shillings)

item.title: El FMI advierte sobre la desaceleración del crecimiento en Asia y del aumento de los rendimientos
item.description: El Fondo Monetario Internacional pronosticó este jueves que el crecimiento económico de Asia se moderará el próximo año y advirtió del aumento de los riesgos derivados de la crisis energética provocada por el conflicto en Oriente Medio, una posible corrección del auge de la inteligencia artificial y las repercusiones del aumento de los rendimientos de los bonos.
item.dc:creator: Leika Kihara
item.content:encoded: El Fondo Monetario Internacional pronosticó este jueves que el crecimiento económico de Asia se moderará el próximo año y advirtió del aumento de los riesgos derivados de la crisis energética provocada por el conflicto en Oriente Medio, una posible corrección del auge de la inteligencia artificial y las repercusiones del aumento de los rendimientos de los bonos. En un informe sobre las perspectivas para la región de Asia-Pacífico, el organismo internacional también señaló que la incertidumbre sobre la trayectoria de la política monetaria de EEUU podría mantener la volatilidad en los mercados financieros asiáticos. "Los tipos de cambio y los flujos de capital se han vuelto más volátiles desde la crisis energética de este año", y varias economías emergentes están experimentando presiones a la depreciación, señaló el FMI en el informe publicado durante sus reuniones anuales en Bangkok. Si bien las entradas de inversión extranjera en la región siguen siendo, en general, sólidas, estos movimientos han coincidido con algunas salidas de carteras, como las de las acciones tecnológicas surcoreanas, señaló. "Se prevé que la política monetaria de EEUU siga endureciéndose este año. Es probable que la combinación del endurecimiento de la política monetaria y las presiones fiscales en la mayoría de las principales economías avanzadas mantenga las presiones al alza sobre los rendimientos en toda Asia y el Pacífico". El FMI señaló que ahora prevé que la economía asiática crezca un 4,8% en 2026 y un 4,4% en 2027, cifras superiores a las previsiones realizadas en abril, aunque siguen representando una desaceleración con respecto a la expansión del 5,0% registrada en 2025. Las revisiones reflejan en gran medida el impulso que supone el auge de la inteligencia artificial para las economías asiáticas avanzadas, cuyo crecimiento se prevé que se acelere hasta el 3,2% en 2026, frente al 2,5% del año pasado, según el informe. Los países emergentes de Asia siguen siendo el principal motor de crecimiento de la región, pero es probable que su crecimiento se modere hasta el 5,1% en 2026, frente al 5,6% del año pasado, debido al impacto del aumento de los precios de la energía, según el informe. "Los riesgos para las perspectivas siguen inclinándose a la baja", ya que un prolongado estancamiento en el conflicto de Oriente Medio podría mantener altos los precios de las materias primas y agotar las reservas de petróleo, señaló el FMI. Una corrección en la demanda de IA podría lastrar el crecimiento mundial, y es probable que los efectos sean especialmente pronunciados en Asia, dada su amplia exposición a la cadena de producción de IA. Con el aumento de los rendimientos a nivel mundial, las tensiones en los mercados de los principales emisores soberanos —como EEUU, Reino Unido, la zona euro y Japón— podrían extenderse a los mercados de bonos asiáticos, lo que haría subir los rendimientos y agravaría las ya elevadas vulnerabilidades fiscales, según el informe. "Dado que la deuda pública y las necesidades de financiación siguen siendo elevadas en gran parte de la región, un endurecimiento brusco de las condiciones financieras podría ejercer una presión adicional sobre las finanzas públicas al aumentar los costos del servicio de la deuda", señaló el FMI. ENFOQUE EN LA ESTABILIDAD DE PRECIOS Las reuniones del FMI de esta semana han estado dominadas por la preocupación por el aumento de la deuda, la subida de los rendimientos de los bonos y los riesgos derivados del auge de la IA. Estas preocupaciones se suman a los quebraderos de cabeza de los responsables políticos por la crisis energética atribuida al conflicto de Oriente Medio, que ha provocado subidas generalizadas de la inflación. El índice bursátil japonés Nikkei (.N225) se desplomaba casi un 5% el jueves, ya que las acciones tecnológicas se vieron muy afectadas por la preocupación sobre la rentabilidad del sector de la IA, mientras que las elevadas cifras de inflación en EEUU despertaron temores de una subida de las tasas de interés. Aunque las expectativas de inflación a largo plazo siguen estando, en general, bien ancladas en Asia, los bancos centrales deberían seguir centrándose en la estabilidad de precios, dijo Krishna Srinivasan, director del Departamento de Asia y el Pacífico del FMI, en una rueda de prensa. "Los bancos centrales deben comunicarse con claridad y estar preparados para endurecer la política monetaria cuando las expectativas estén menos ancladas, los marcos sean menos creíbles o la inflación sea más persistente. Para respaldar esto, debe mantenerse la independencia de los bancos centrales", dijo. Dado que la deuda pública se mantiene por encima de los niveles previos a la pandemia, el margen para un gasto fiscal adicional es cada vez más limitado, señaló Srinivasan. La política fiscal debería ser selectiva y temporal, añadió, e instó a los países de la región a evitar los subsidios generales a los combustibles o los controles de precios, que podrían resultar más costosos.

item.title: India’s bank privatisation offers cautious win-win
item.description: Canada’s Fairfax is set to acquire 61% of IDBI Bank for $5.6 bln, the largest foreign bet on an Indian lender. For the buyer, it's a cheap valuation and it delivers an okay return for state rescuer LIC. But the deal will test whether New Delhi is really willing to stand back.
item.dc:creator: Ujjaini Dutta
item.content:encoded: After a decade of dithering, New Delhi looks poised to check the privatisation of IDBI Bank (IDBI.NS) off its to-do list. Canada's Fairfax Financial (FFH.TO) is set to buy 61% of the lender for 529 billion rupees ($5.6 billion) in India's largest cross-border bank deal. It offers the buyer’s founder, Prem Watsa, a chance to build a leading private sector institution if the government stays out of his way. It was 2016 when New Delhi first floated the idea of cutting its stake in IDBI from 80% to below 50%. The government and state-controlled Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIFI.NS) will each offload a roughly 30% stake. They’ll partly cash out of the thinly traded and volatile shares at a 10% discount to the last closing price on Wednesday, the day before officials named Prem Watsa’s company as their preferred “strategic buyer”. There’s no binding agreement but if the deal goes through, it'll be a remarkable full circle for a bank that was one of the hardest hit by a nationwide asset quality crisis. Around 2019, IDBI's gross non-performing loans stood at nearly one-third of its portfolio. That prompted the government to nudge LIC to pump in 216 billion rupees, or $2.3 billion at current exchange rates, to raise its 8% stake to 51% in 2019. Today, bad loans are just 2.3% of IDBI’s book. Fairfax looks well placed to build on that repair. It’s paying a multiple of around 1 times IDBI’s trailing book value. A well-run private sector bank with better tech savvy like ICICI Bank (ICBK.NS) commands 2.5 times. Fairfax will combine IDBI with its non-bank lender $1.1 billion IIFL Capital Services (IIFS.NS) and insurer Digit to cross-sell banking, insurance and financial services products. For LIC, the deal crystallises a 7.44% annualised price return on its 2019 investment. That is less than ideal compared to the 10% yielded by India’s benchmark Nifty 50 stock Index (.NSEI) over the period but for New Delhi, it is not a terrible price to pay to stop a bank from going under. The sellers will gain in two more ways. Offloading IDBI will bring some fiscal relief for the government firefighting surging oil prices and help it hit its annual target for divestment for the first time in seven years. They'll also have a chance to improve their returns: LIC and the government will withdraw from the board but retain a combined stake of 34%, higher than the 26% regulatory cap on voting rights Fairfax will be subject to as a private owner of an Indian bank. That offers plenty of upside so long as officials can resist meddling. Follow Ujjaini Dutta on LinkedIn and X . Canada's Fairfax Financial Holdings is set to buy 60.7% of India's IDBI Bank for 528.78 billion rupees ($5.56 billion), the Indian government said in a press release on October 14. The government named Fairfax as its preferred strategic buyer but no binding agreements have been signed. If a deal goes through, it would represent the largest foreign direct investment into the financial sector. New Delhi and state-controlled Life Insurance Corp of India will each sell a roughly 30% stake. The government will retain a 15% stake and LIC a 19% stake after the transaction. They will withdraw from the bank's board and become public shareholders. Fairfax will offer 81 rupees per share for IDBI Bank. The price is above the benchmark price of 75.99 rupees per share determined by the government based on fair valuations but a discount of 10% to the closing price of 90.39 rupees on October 14. India first said it would consider cutting its stake in IDBI Bank from around 80% to below 50% in February 2016. LIC started increasing its stake around that time. In 2019, LIC became the majority owner. Around that time, the bank's gross non-performing loans amounted to nearly 30% of its total assets. CONTEXT-NEWS

item.title: Pernod Ricard-Le CA recule moins que prévu au T1, les USA et la Chine pèsent toujours
item.description: Pernod Ricard a fait état jeudi d'une baisse moins importante que prévu de son chiffre d'affaires au premier trimestre, le groupe de spiritueux accusant, comme anticipé, d'importants reculs en Chine et aux États-Unis.
item.dc:creator: Etienne Breban
item.content:encoded: Pernod Ricard (PERP.PA) a fait état jeudi d'une baisse moins importante que prévu de son chiffre d'affaires au premier trimestre, le groupe de spiritueux accusant, comme anticipé, d'importants reculs en Chine et aux États-Unis. Sur les trois premiers mois de son exercice, Pernod Ricard affiche un chiffre d'affaires en recul organique de 0,9% sur un an, à 2,23 milliards d'euros, alors que les analystes tablaient en moyenne sur un recul de 1,7% de ses revenus, selon un consensus compilé par le groupe. En août, Pernod Ricard [USN:L8N44O08S TEXT:"avait déclaré"] prévoir un recul de ses ventes en Chine et aux États-Unis en raison d'ajustements de stocks. Sur ces deux marchés, les chiffre d'affaires sont respectivement en baisse de 25% et 10% au premier trimestre. Lors des résultats annuels, le président-directeur général, Alexandre Ricard, avait alors souligné ne pas prévoir un retour à la croissance sur le marché américain avant 2029. En Chine en revanche, le groupe a avancé jeudi un "optimisme prudent" des distributeurs à l'approche de la Fête de la Mi-Automne, alors que les ventes aux distributeurs (depletions) sont de retour à la croissance dans le pays. Dans la région "Reste du Monde", hors États-Unis et Chine, le chiffre d’affaires de la maison-mère du cognac Martell, du champagne Mumm et de la vodka Absolut progresse de +4% sur le trimestre. Il avance de 19% sur un an en Inde, où Pernod Ricard India envisage une introduction en Bourse (IPO), mais recule de 6% en Europe. "Même si la faiblesse du marché européen pourrait retenir l'attention, les ventes aux distributeurs en Chine et les déclarations sur les États-Unis sont encourageants", ont observé les analystes de JP Morgan dans une note. "Les pessimistes mettront en avant la faiblesse des tendances en Europe et le fait que la forte croissance de l’Inde inclut une partie des commandes passées en prévision de l'IPO", estiment quant à eux les analystes de Jefferies "Toutefois, ces résultats devraient être suffisants, car ils renforcent la confiance des investisseurs quant à la fin du cycle de révision à la baisse." À l'ouverture des marchés à Paris, l'action Pernod Ricard prenait environ 3% à 67,6 euros. Pernod Ricard confirme par ailleurs ses objectifs annuels et à moyen terme, dont un chiffre d’affaires organique "globalement stable" en 2027.

item.title: Macron va effectuer une tournée dans le Golfe, sécurité et énergie au menu
item.description: Emmanuel Macron effectuera en début de semaine prochaine une tournée dans le Golfe afin de "poursuivre sa mobilisation" auprès de dirigeants régionaux pour revenir à la stabilité et à la libre circulation dans le détroit d'Ormuz, voie cruciale pour les livraisons énergétiques mondiales, a dit mercredi l'Elysée.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Emmanuel Macron effectuera en début de semaine prochaine une tournée dans le Golfe afin de "poursuivre sa mobilisation" auprès de dirigeants régionaux pour revenir à la stabilité et à la libre circulation dans le détroit d'Ormuz, voie cruciale pour les livraisons énergétiques mondiales, a dit mercredi l'Elysée. Le chef de l'Etat se rendra au Koweït, aux Émirats arabes unis, à Bahreïn et au Qatar du 19 au 21 octobre, a fait savoir la présidence française dans un communiqué. Les discussions concerneront notamment "la sécurisation et la diversification de nos approvisionnements énergétiques et de leurs voies d'acheminement", est-il écrit. "Il s'agit de limiter les conséquences de la crise énergétique sur le quotidien des Français". Emmanuel Macron veut également "renforcer les partenariats stratégiques et économiques que la France entretient avec les pays du Golfe", a déclaré l'Elysée, et "renforcer nos coopérations en matière d'énergie, d'enjeux globaux, de défense et de sécurité". Des entretiens bilatéraux sont prévus avec l'émir du Koweït, le président des Emirats arabes unis, le roi du Bahreïn et l'émir du Qatar.

item.title: Pernod Ricard first quarter sales fall less-than-expected, cautious optimism on China
item.description: Pernod Ricard on Thursday reported a smaller-than- expected 0.9% drop in sales for the first quarter of its 2027 fiscal year, impacted by weak demand and de-stocking in China and the United States although demand in India was strong.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Pernod Ricard (PERP.PA) on Thursday reported a smaller-than- expected 0.9% drop in sales for the first quarter of its 2027 fiscal year, impacted by weak demand and de-stocking in China and the United States although demand in India was strong. Pernod, the world's second-largest spirits maker after Diageo (DGE.L) , said underlying trends in China were improving, confirming its cautious optimism ahead of the Chinese Mid-Autumn festival. Pernod also reiterated a forecast for broadly stable net sales in the current fiscal year started on July 1. The maker of Martell cognac and Absolut vodka, which held unsuccessful merger talks with Jack Daniel's maker Brown-Forman earlier this year, reported Q1 sales of 2.234 billion euros ($2.51 billion), an organic decline of 0.9% against estimates of a 1.7% decline in a company-compiled poll of analysts. Sales fell 10% in the United States and 25% in China but rose 19 in India in the first quarter. In India the group has said it was taking preparatory steps to a potential IPO. It reiterated the decision to proceed to an IPO remains subject to board approval. Pernod also said it will strongly defend its organic operating margin supported by strict cost control. Pernod also reiterated it expects sales growth at the lower end of its 3% to 6% target range through 2029, underscoring the prolonged downturn facing global spirits makers. Spirits makers across the industry are grappling with a multi-year sales downturn that has eroded valuations, triggered management changes and prompted asset sales and cost-cutting. ($1 = 0.8917 euros)
